newsitem.title: USA: OPEC mulls raising crude target price - Lukman.
newsitem.headline: OPEC mulls raising crude target price - Lukman.

text.p: OPEC Secretary General Rilwanu Lukman said Tuesday that higher crude oil prices could prompt the cartel to raise its target price from the current $21 a barrel.
"If we have sustained higher prices, then we may have to look at that target price," Lukman said in a speech at an energy forum in Houston.

The average price of OPEC's basket of crude oil rose to $23.23 a barrel in January from $18.06 a barrel in January 1996, prompting Lukman to question whether the increase was temporary or marked a new "threshold" for oil prices.
The target price set by the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries is used as a barometer by oil ministers of its 13 member countries.
"Price is like a thermometer. It tells us what is happening in the market," Lukman said.

He told reporters OPEC has been approached by some producing countries in the former Soviet Union, Africa and Latin America about joining the cartel. "It would be premature for me to divulge the names," he said.
"We are hopeful that even if no other countries are added to OPEC, the level of cooperation between us and non-OPEC countries is increasing," Lukman told reporters after his speech.
The Vienna, Austria-based organisation also wants to establish closer ties to consuming countries to assess oil demand and set production quotas.
"People are talking a more common language now and trying to iron out the rough spots of supply and demand," he said.
